response.answer: Numerical stability in matrix exponential computation is guaranteed by adaptive λ selection and Padé approximation with fallback criteria. Runtime tradeoffs involve balancing accuracy and computational cost. Scipy's expm uses a variable order Padé approximation for this purpose.

If the input data is not of single and double precision of real and complex dtypes, it is copied to a new array. For cases `n>= 400`, the exact 1-norm computation cost, breaks even with 1-norm estimation and from that point on the estimation scheme given in [2] is used to decide on the approximation order. results.title: expm (MATLAB Function Reference)
results.content: `Y = expm(X)`  raises the constant *e* to the matrix power `X.` Complex results are produced if `X` has nonpositive eigenvalues. The `expm` function is built-in, but it uses the Padé approximation with scaling and squaring algorithm expressed in the file `expm1.m`. A second method of calculating the matrix exponential uses a Taylor series approximation. This method is demonstrated in the file `expm2.m`. A third way of calculating the matrix exponential, found in the file `expm3.m`, is to diagonalize the matrix, apply the function to the individual eigenvalues, and then transform back. This method fails if the input matrix does not have a full set of linearly independent eigenvectors. Suppose `A` is the 3-by-3 matrix. Notice that the diagonal elements of the two results are equal; this would be true for any triangular matrix. `funm`Evaluate functions of a matrix. F. Van Loan, *Matrix Computation*, p. F. Van Loan, "Nineteen Dubious Ways to Compute the Exponential of a Matrix," *SIAM Review 20*, 1979, pp.
